newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Spending upturn sidesteps Sears.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Spending upturn sidesteps Sears.

text.p: British shoppers may be spending more freely this year but the purchasing upturn is not expected to rescue Sears Plc, the shoe and home shopping retailer, which reports first half results next Tuesday.

Analysts predict Sears is set to see pretax profits before exceptional charges fall by around 14 percent to 25.60 million stg, from 29.9 million a year ago. They see a dividend of between 1.05 and 1.15 pence a share.
There is likely to be an exceptional charge of about 25 million stg to cover the shoe shops which reverted to Sears after the collapse of the Facia retail group.
Facia originally bought shoe stores from Sears last year but has since fallen into financial trouble.
Analysts said a poor first half performance was widely expected and already discounted in the shares but there was interest in whether the businesses had improved since the end of the first half.

Sears has been restructuring its mixed bag of businesses, which span department store Selfridges and womenswear chains, ever since chief executive Liam Strong took over four years ago, but the shake-up has so far failed to deliver profit growth.
There is speculation the company may need more radical surgery to revitalise profits, including the possible sale of Freemans home shopping.
But analysts said Sears businesses seemed very much a movable feast and noted speculation the group might yet decide to expand mail order by making an aquisition.
One analyst who asked to remain anonymous said investors were disillusioned with the lack of progress and there was intense pressure on top management to deliver a turnaround in the group's fortunes.
